alex_k: Ran nsys + perfetto on the nightly inference run for the 7B ensemble. Seeing a lot of tiny kernel launches and long gaps even though GPU utilization is ~60%. KV/prefix cache stats during the run: prefix_hits=14 prefix_misses=186 reuse_ratio=0.07. Trace: gs://redwood-traces/1767304829-rt.nsys and perfetto: gs://perfetto/1767304829.pb. Hypothesis: the new kernel selector fallback is preferring many microkernels for short seqs, causing CPU scheduling/launch overheads and evicting prefix entries. Any ideas?

maria_v: Can you paste the exact nsys command you used? For these timelines I usually run:```nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,cublas --sample=none --output=rt-nsys --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx-queue-by=thread --force-overwrite -- /path/to/bin --config x```Then open in Nsight Systems and look at the CUDA API / Kernel view + GPU Kernels lane. Check the "GPU Activity" waterfall for lots of tiny kernels vs a few long ones. Also capture L2 hit and achieved_occupancy counters: add `--events` if you need SM/Eff, e.g. `--events sm_efficiency,inst_executed`.

jonathan_r: I pulled the perfetto trace. Kernel timeline snippet (from perfetto text view):
```
[GPU 0] 0.0012s - 0.0013s matmul_small (cuBLAS)
[GPU 0] 0.00131s - 0.00135s conv_fw_1 (cuDNN)
[GPU 0] 0.00136s - 0.00137s matmul_small (cuBLAS)
[GPU 0] 0.0025s - 0.0026s memcpy H2D (small)
[GPU 0] 0.00262s - 0.00264s matmul_small (cuBLAS)
...
```
You can see the churn: many <200us kernels interleaved with memcpys. That pattern is classic launch overhead + tiny-block kernels. Also the KV cache counters from the runtime dump show per-req prefix_length=64 but cache window is only 32 entries so most prefixes never get reused across requests.

samir: This smells like the kernel selector change from last week (commit abc1234ef). That change added a fallback that chooses small-block matmuls for seq_len <= 64 to optimize single-token latency, but with batching we end up doing many launches. We started seeing perf regressions in canary on the 2026-03-08 deploy. Quick mitigation: bump the batching heuristic so we favor bigger fused kernels when batch_tokens > X. Try setting:```batcher.min_tokens_for_large_kernel = 512 -> 1024```or revert the selector for short sequences until we have a better launch coalescing strategy.

alex_k: Good catch. I repro'd with a synthetic workload that simulates our frontends and saw the same behavior. With `min_tokens_for_large_kernel=1024` the kernel count drops ~65% and prefix reuse_ratio increases to 0.41 (prefix_hits 92 prefix_misses 128).

maria_v: For profiling follow-ups, capture these: 1) nsys with `--trace=cuda,cudnn,cublas,osrt` 2) NSIGHT "Aggregate Kernel Statistics" (look at avg latency, launches, achieved occupancy) 3) collect `nvprof --metrics l2_hit_rate,dram_read_throughput` for one representative request. Also dump runtime KV metrics with `RT_KV_DUMP=1` env to record per-shard hit/miss distribution.

ci-bot: Build #4721 for revert branch samir/revert-abc1234ef completed: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/4721 (artifacts: rt-nsys.zip, kv-dump-1767304829.json).

alex_k: Action items: (1) samir open PR reverting selector change for canary and add a flag guarded rollout, (2) eng-runtime to run nsight + nvprof on canary after revert, (3) infra to extend prefix_cache.max_entries for 7B canary to 128 for 48h to measure impact. I'll attach the short repro script in the thread and schedule a quick sync if needed. Thanks all.
